business_scope.primary_industry_name: Deep-Sea Tugboat Towage and Maritime Emergency Salvage Contracts

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (IPPA) between ARATS and SEF, signed August 31, 2012
Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA), signed June 29, 2010

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (latest revision adopted November 8, 2024, effective January 1, 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (effective July 1, 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2020); Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration (State Council Decree No. 746); Enterprise Name Registration Administration Provisions (SAMR Order, effective March 1, 2021); Tax Registration Measures with the State Taxation Administration; and cross-strait SEF/ARATS document verification procedures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Register Extract) of the Taiwanese investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan Company and Commerce Registration Bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only (Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille party): Taiwan district court notarization of the certified copy, then authentication by the Taiwan MOEA, then verification by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), then verification by the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS), and final legalization by the PRC consular office if required by the receiving authority; no Hague Apostille may be applied.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of No Dissolution from the Taiwan Corporate Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan Department of Commerce / Company and Commerce Registration Bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: court notarization, MOEA authentication, SEF verification, ARATS verification, and PRC consular legalization if applicable; Hague Apostille is inapplicable and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE legal representative and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan parent company, notarized by a Taiwan district court public notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: notarization by the Taiwan district court, authentication by MOEA, SEF verification, ARATS verification, and PRC consular legalization as required; no apostille, no hybrid chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Constitution) of the Taiwan parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan parent company, with notarization by the Taiwan district court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: notarization, MOEA authentication if required, SEF verification, ARATS verification, PRC consular legalization; Hague Apostille not available.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the Taiwan parent company's principal banking institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan commercial bank approved under the Banking Act of Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: bank officer's notarized signature with bank seal, Taiwan district court notarization if required, SEF verification, ARATS verification, and PRC consular legalization; no apostille, and no sequential layering with the Hague Convention.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), Articles 98–113 (Limited Company), Article 387 (company registration), and Article 5 (central competent authority); administered together with the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, Article 73, and the Regulations on the Permission of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland People; the business scope remains subject to the Negative List for Mainland Investment issued by the Investment Commission.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan; online filing through the MOEA One-Stop Company and Commerce Application System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application Form together with the Articles of Incorporation, an authenticated written Shareholder Consent, and the Director's Consent to Serve.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Taiwan limited company after the 2018 Company Act amendment; the sole shareholder must subscribe the full declared capital (NT$16,000,000) and remit it into a Taiwan bank account prior to filing. No statutory escrow account is mandated, but the Investment Commission requires the inward remittance receipt/capital verification certificate and restricts withdrawal of funds for any purpose outside the approved business scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED at the first meeting of the Sole Shareholder and initial Director of the Company: (i) the Sole Shareholder subscribes in full to the paid-in capital of NT$16,000,000 for 16,000,000 shares, payable in cash into the Company's bank account; (ii) the registered office of the Company is adopted at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation and shall be used for all Company registrations; (iii) Ms./Mr. [Name] is appointed Director/President and Ms./Mr. [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer and Administrative Officer, with full authority to open bank accounts, sign contracts, and file statutory returns; (iv) the Company shall immediately apply for its Maritime Port registration, business registration, and all industrial licenses; and (v) this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mainland Investment Approval and Negative-List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission (Department of Investment Review), Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, via the MOEA Invest Taiwan / Direct Investment application portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Mainland-Investor investment application before any Taiwan company registration. Provide the mainland parent's corporate certificate and audited financial statements, a detailed business plan for deep-sea tugboat towage and maritime emergency salvage (ISIC 5222), the proposed Taiwan company name, capital structure, and registered address. The Investment Commission reviews national security, economic impact, and the mainland negative list. Obtain the written investment permit, which must be presented to Taiwanese banks for capital remittance and to the registry for incorporation.
required_dossiers: Mainland investor incorporation/business certificate
Audited financial statements of the mainland investor for the last fiscal year
Mainland Investment Application form
Business plan for ISIC 5222 towage/salvage and operational safety statement
Proposed Taiwan company name, capital, and shareholding schedule
Power of attorney to the local Taiwan filing agent
Declaration of no negative-list restriction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An application query is cured by filing supplementary explanations within 30 days; a conditional approval may restrict the operational scope (e.g., international waters or non-Taiwan-flagged vessels). A formal refusal may be appealed to the Executive Yuan under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days, or the applicant may restructure the business scope and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Inward Capital Remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA online name-reservation system; inward remittance via an approved Taiwan bank under the Central Bank Foreign Exchange Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the Chinese company name and optional English name online; the registry checks collision and wording restrictions. After the Investment Commission permit is issued, open a provisional company capital account at a Taiwan bank, submit the permit, execute the Foreign Exchange Declaration for Direct Investment, and remit the approved NT$16,000,000. The bank issues a Capital Verification Certificate, which is indispensable for the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission permit letter
Foreign exchange remittance application (direct investment declaration)
Bank account opening package with beneficial ownership declaration
Source-of-funds documentation (board resolution and bank statements of the mainland parent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, reserve a new name, which is processed within 1–2 working days. If the bank or central bank queries the remittance, provide the permit and updated source-of-funds evidence; any return of funds requires prior foreign-exchange approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Authentication, and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Notary Public / court notary office, with the Department of Commercial Affairs for form compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Mandarin Chinese, with an English courtesy translation, containing the company name, object (deep-sea tugboat towage and maritime salvage), paid-in capital, share structure, registered address, single-director structure, and governing law. The sole shareholder signs the written Shareholder Consent; the initial director signs the Consent to Serve. If any document originates from mainland China, arrange the required cross-strait authentication and verify the signatories before a Taiwan notary where required.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation (Chinese text)
Shareholders' written consent approving incorporation and capital
Initial director's consent to serve with ID copies
Power of attorney / corporate resolution of the mainland parent
Proof of registered office (lease or ownership title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notary or registry objections are cured by redrafting non-compliant clauses to meet mandatory Company Act provisions and resubmitting; authentication defects are corrected by obtaining the proper cross-strait attestation or court notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Registration with the Department of Commercial Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, via the One-Stop Company and Commerce Online Application System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Establishment Registration Application Form online together with the Articles, shareholder consent, director consent, capital verification certificate, Investment Commission permit, proof of registered office, and seal registration forms. The authority examines name, capital, scope, and compliance; upon approval the Ministry issues the Company Registration Certificate and publishes the registration record.
required_dossiers: Company Establishment Registration Application Form
Articles of Incorporation (notarized)
Shareholders' written consent/minutes
Director's consent and responsible-person ID
Bank Capital Verification Certificate
Investment Commission permit letter
Proof of registered office address
Company chop and responsible-person chop registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A query letter allows a 15-day curing period to file supplementary documents; a refusal is appealable to the Ministry of Economic Affairs or the Executive Yuan, or the applicant may correct the objection and re-file a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Uniform Invoice Entitlement, and Responsible-Person Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Administration (local branch, e.g., Taipei National Taxation Administration) and the municipal business registration unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of the company registration, file the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax registration, obtain the Taxpayer Identification Number, and register the responsible person and company seal. Apply for uniform-invoice entitlement and confirm the applicable tax category. Any port-operation registration required by the harbor authority should be coordinated with this tax registration.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Investment Commission permit letter
Articles of Incorporation
Responsible-person identification document
Power of attorney for the filing agent
Bank statement and capital verification record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late-filing penalties are cured by immediate filing and payment of the nominal fine; mismatches between tax-registration scope and company scope are cured by a tax amendment filing aligned to the registration certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime Port Licensing, Vessel Registration, and Operating Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Maritime Port Bureau, Ministry of Transportation and Communications, Taiwan, in coordination with the local commercial harbor administration (e.g., Keelung/Taipei or Kaohsiung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the auxiliary maritime transport service registration for tugboat towage and vessel salvage under the Shipping Act and the Commercial Port Act. Submit the company registration and tax certificates, the Investment Commission permit, P&I and hull/machinery insurance certificates, vessel ownership or valid bareboat charter documents, crew qualification evidence, and an emergency-response/salvage operational plan. Each tug and salvage vessel requires a separate Vessel Registration Certificate and valid safety certificates (load line, SOLAS, manning). For port calls, obtain the harbor authority entry approval.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate and tax registration
Investment Commission permit covering ISIC 5222 scope
Vessel ownership certificates or bareboat charter agreements
P&I / hull and machinery insurance certificates
Salvage and towage operational and emergency-response plan
Crew licenses and vessel safety/manning certificates
Harbor authority operating/entry permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is queried, the applicant supplies missing classification or vessel certificates, or narrows the operating area (e.g., international waters only). An adverse decision may be cured by re-filing with corrected documentation or by administrative appeal to the MOTC within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Maritime Port Bureau, Ministry of Transportation and Communications, Taiwan, as the competent shipping and port authority under the Shipping Act and the Commercial Port Act; jointly with the Ministry of Economic Affairs Industrial Development Administration for any shore-side industrial works.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Auxiliary Maritime Transport Service Registration and Operating Permit — Deep-Sea Tugboat Towage and Vessel Salvage issued under the Shipping Act and Commercial Port Act, together with Vessel Registration Certificates and Manning Certificates for all tugs and salvage craft.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan, with delegated local environmental protection bureaus
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Vessel-based towage/salvage without shore-side construction is generally exempt from a full EIA; the installation of a shore facility, fuel storage, repair yard, or dredging triggers a Category B Initial Environmental Check or a Category A Full Environmental Impact Assessment under Article 5 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Vessels must comply with the Marine Pollution Control Act, the Water Pollution Control Act, and MARPOL 73/78 as ratified by Taiwan: zero oil or oily-mixture discharge (15 ppm oily-water separator threshold); treated sewage discharge only beyond 3 nautical miles; Annex V garbage retention; marine fuel sulphur content ≤ 0.50% m/m under Annex VI; compliance with harbor-area emissions and VOC/waste-handling rules; and an approved oil-spill emergency plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification by the local Fire Bureau for office, workshop, and fuel-storage premises; structural load inspection certificates for any shore-side berthing, warehouse, or maintenance facility; occupational safety and health clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act administered by the Ministry of Labor; personnel manning and seafarer competence certificates verified by the Maritime Port Bureau; and port-area emergency-response and oil-spill contingency approval.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, functioning as the FX-control and cross-border payment regulatory authority under the People's Bank of China (PBOC); cross-strait Taiwan investment is additionally coordinated through the MOFCOM Department of Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macao Affairs and the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, with Taiwan-origin RMB clearing channeled through Bank of China Taipei branch and the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC maintains current-account convertibility for trade in services, which includes deep-sea towage hire and maritime salvage awards; all current-account receipts and payments must be supported by a genuine underlying transaction, a commercial contract, invoice, or arbitral award, and must settle through SAFE-supervised designated banks. Capital-account items—FDI equity injection, shareholder loans, and liquidation or capital-reduction repatriation—remain subject to prior SAFE filing/registration, real-demand authentication, and negative-list compliance. For a Taiwan-invested WFOE, after-tax distributable profits may be remitted to the Taiwan parent under the current-account 'investment income' head upon presentation of audited financial statements, the corporate income tax final-settlement certificate, the dividend withholding tax certificate, and the bank's SAFE verification; no fixed repatriation cap applies, but the remittance documentation must be complete at the bank counter. Liquidation proceeds, equity-transfer consideration, and repayment of foreign shareholder loans are capital-account flows requiring SAFE registration and case-by-case review, with processing time of several weeks. Inbound salvage awards under Lloyd's Open Form (LOF 2011) and emergency towage fees are classifiable as current-account 'maritime transport and salvage services' income; convertibility to RMB and onward disbursement is administratively feasible when the contract, the salvage award or security agreement, and the P&I club letter of undertaking are produced. Full RMB convertibility for speculative or capital-account purposes is not available; the WFOE must operate strictly through the onshore FX market.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China abolished mandatory FX surrender in 2012; there is no statutory conversion ratio for export or service-fee proceeds. The controlling obligation is repatriation plus SAFE verification: the WFOE must bring towage and salvage receivables into its onshore current-account foreign exchange account through a designated bank, and the bank must report the credit to SAFE within five working days of settlement using the trade-in-services verification module. For service-export contracts, the collection period is the contractual credit term; a receipt more than 180 days after the invoice or service-completion date must be flagged to SAFE with a written explanation and debt-collection evidence. For incidental goods exports (e.g., sale of surplus salvage equipment or condemned vessel parts), the goods-export proceeds must enter the SAFE trade-monitoring system within 90 days of the customs export declaration, and extended collection periods must be pre-registered with the local SAFE branch. The WFOE may retain 100% of its FX receipts in the account or convert to RMB at will; any conversion and every subsequent payment from the RMB settlement-pending account must be matched to a genuine business purpose with invoices. RMB-denominated receipts from Taiwan counterparties must be reported through RCPMIS by the settlement bank; Taiwan legal and natural persons are treated under special compatriot investment rules, but treasury receipts are subject to the same trade-verification framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI FX capital fund account (capital escrow) + current-account FX account + RMB basic deposit account; sole mainland RMB clearing channel for Taiwan-origin RMB

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI FX capital fund account + current-account FX account + trade-finance lines
RMB basic operational account + current-account FX account; dedicated maritime and shipping industry division
RMB basic deposit account + current-account FX account + NAFMII derivatives line for FX hedging
RMB basic deposit account + cross-border RMB account (CIPS) for Taiwan-origin settlement
RMB basic deposit account + current-account FX account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low, with only ancillary application. Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Currenxie, WorldFirst, Payoneer) cannot lawfully replace SAFE-regulated onshore settlement for a China-incorporated WFOE: towage-fee and salvage receivables must be credited to the WFOE's onshore current-account FX account and reported by the designated bank to SAFE. A mainland entity cannot open a general-purpose offshore EMI account without SAFE 'overseas account' approval, and routing Taiwan parent capital injections or client charges through an offshore EMI would breach RCPMIS reporting and SAFE trade-verification rules. For USD-multi-million invoices, P&I club security deposits, and LOF award wires, the EMI rail is operationally and legally non-viable. A Shanghai Free Trade Zone or Hainan FTP-registered WFOE may obtain a Free Trade Account (FT account) at a licensed bank, which offers onshore-offshore flexibility similar to an EMI but with full SAFE supervision; no unlicensed EMI is permitted to hold the WFOE's operating treasury.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is effectively mandatory for a Taiwan-invested WFOE. Under PBOC Order No.1/2018 (Customer Identification and Client Due Diligence Measures) and the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law, the legal representative, the Taiwan investor's designated director, and every UBO must be identified through a face-to-face interview at the bank counter; the bank must retain the 'dual-recording' (audio-video) interview file for primary accounts. Exceptions permitting fully remote video opening apply only to basic RMB accounts of small enterprises in selected pilot cities and never extend to FX capital-fund accounts. The Taiwan shareholder may delegate signatory authority through a power of attorney notarized in Taiwan and channelized through the SEF/ARATS process or through a mainland notary, with the authorized officer physically attending bank counters; in practice, tier-1 banks additionally require the mainland legal representative to appear in person for the current-account FX account and the FDI capital-fund account, or require a mainland counsel-attested specimen of company chops and signatures. Digital account opening is not available for foreign-invested enterprise accounts with capital-account functions in the current regulatory environment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layer Taiwan/Hong Kong holding structure with an intermediate entity lacking commercial substance, making beneficial ownership tracing difficult.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organizational chart showing the full shareholding chain to the ultimate natural person; certificate of incorporation and articles of association of every intermediate entity; latest audited financial statements of each holding layer; the WFOE's business license and approval/filing certificate; board resolutions of all layers authorizing the banking mandate and nominated signatories; Taiwan Compatriot Permit or passport copies of all UBOs; corporate registry extracts dated within 90 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque offshore maritime client base: shipowners registered under flags of convenience (Panama, Marshall Islands, Liberia), with payment offered by a third-party P&I club, charterer, or security trustee rather than the direct contractual debtor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed BIMCO TOWCON/TOWHIRE or LOF 2011 salvage agreement identifying the vessel by name and IMO number and the exact billing party; vessel flag registry certificate and IMO tonnage certificate; third-party payment authority letter from the contractual debtor; bank reference letter from the payer's bank; prior 12 months of bank statements demonstrating a consistent pattern of similar maritime receipts; voyage orders and any relevant letter of indemnity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large one-off salvage award or arbitration proceeds from Lloyd's Salvage Arbitration Branch or a Chinese maritime court, with non-routine high-value credit activity inconsistent with ordinary towage hire.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Lloyd's Standard Form of Salvage Agreement; final arbitration award or interim LOF security document; salvor's operational log and casualty timeline; International Group P&I club letter of undertaking; marine insurance policy declarations; certified Chinese translation of the award; explanatory board resolution approving the receipt and its treasury allocation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure arising from towage/salvage operations in contested waters, ports in high-risk jurisdictions, or the involvement of vessels appearing on UN, OFAC, or EU sanctions lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UN/OFAC/EU sanctions screening reports (World-Check or Dow Jones risk screen) for all counterparties and vessel IMOS; contractual sanctions-termination and no-transshipment clauses; the WFOE's written sanctions-compliance policy and staff AML training records; written confirmation from the client's P&I club that no sanctioned party is involved; completed 'no-touch' attestations for Iranian, Russian, Cuban, North Korean, and Syrian exposures; service-entry certificates from the local maritime administration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disbursement layering to unrelated subcontractors such as bunker suppliers, sub-tug operators, crew agencies, and equipment vendors, creating fragmentation and laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original invoices showing bank details; back-to-back subcontract agreements; voyage disbursement account (VDA) reports from the master or manning agent; master's disbursement requests; written authorization from the towage contract owner; the tax filing voucher for outward service payments for each disbursement exceeding USD 50,000; crew payroll lists with seafarer certificates; evidence of tax withholding where required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for Taiwan parent to WFOE equity injection: (1) complete the Taiwan-investment filing at the local MOFCOM/Taiwan Affairs competent authority and obtain the WFOE business license; (2) complete the FDI FX registration at the designated bank under the direct registration system, using SAFE receipt code '622010' (inbound FDI equity contribution in currency) with counterpart jurisdiction 'TW'; (3) open a distinct FDI foreign exchange capital fund account segregated from current-account FX accounts; (4) the Taiwan parent remits TWD, USD, or RMB via SWIFT MT103 with the remittance narrative stating 'investment contribution' and quoting the SAFE FDI registration number; (5) upon credit, the bank files the receipt with SAFE and classifies the funds strictly as foreign-exchange capital; (6) conversion of capital into RMB operates under the voluntary-settlement regime, with the bank crediting an RMB settlement-pending-payment account; every onward payment from that account must be invoice-backed and business-purpose verified, and is prohibited for onshore securities, speculative equity or trust investments, non-own-use real estate, and on-lending; (7) for RMB remittances from Taiwan, settlement clears through Bank of China Taipei branch/CIPS and must be reported via RCPMIS by the receiving bank. No minimum paid-in capital is imposed by law, but the registered capital amount in the MOFCOM filing must be received within the undertaking period, and any injection exceeding the registered capital requires separate SAFE approval. Under LOF 2011, the salvage award wire is treated not as capital but as current-account service income; the crediting bank requires the signed LOF agreement and the arbitral award to complete trade verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Standard clearing rails for the WFOE's payment obligations: (a) ordinary maritime operating payments (bunkers, port dues, crew wages, subcontract towage, P&I premiums, and repairs) are effected by SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the current-account FX account; for each service payment exceeding USD 50,000 or the RMB equivalent, the bank requires the outward-services tax filing voucher from the tax authority and withholds applicable corporate income tax and withholding tax at source; (b) cross-border RMB payments to Taiwan suppliers and sub-tug operators are cleared via CIPS or Taiwan agent banks and reported through RCPMIS; (c) large capital procurement (e.g., construction of a new escort tug, heavy salvaging gear, submersible pumps) should be routed through an irrevocable sight commercial letter of credit issued by the WFOE's bank (SWIFT MT700/MT720) and confirmed by the overseas beneficiary's bank to eliminate prepayment risk; (d) disbursements to overseas co-salvors and tug beneficiaries secured under a LOF escrow are released only upon presentation of the Lloyd's award, a P&I club release instruction, or a jointly signed disbursement authority; the bank records the escrow debit instruction and attaches the supporting release document; (e) all outbound payments must match the negative list and be recorded in the annual SAFE/BOP filing, with the bank reporting each cross-border debit to SAFE within five working days of payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore CNY foreign exchange forwards (forward settlement and sale of foreign exchange) for current-account exposures such as USD/EUR towage receivables and subcontract payables, executed under a NAFMII FX master agreement with the onboarded bank; SAFE real-demand verification requires documentary evidence of the underlying trade exposure and matching of forecasted cash flows.
RMB/foreign-currency cross-currency interest rate swaps for medium-term balance-sheet hedging where the WFOE holds cross-currency liabilities, capital injections, or staged equipment payments.

Buy-side onshore FX options and zero-net-premium option structures (e.g., forward-plus-option combinations); writing or selling options is prohibited for non-financial corporate clients, and the structures must be supported by genuine exposure.

Onshore FX swaps for temporary conversion of FX receipts into RMB for payroll and local disbursement while preserving the ability to reconvert for future FX payables; each leg requires underlying transaction documentation.

NDFs are not permissible for the onshore WFOE's own treasury book; offshore NDF execution is available only to the Taiwan parent in offshore markets such as Hong Kong or Singapore and must not be booked on the WFOE balance sheet; the compliant onshore alternative is a deliverable forward tied to actual receivables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting and Financial Statements Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (typically by 30 June; extension possible)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: New Taiwan Dollar (TWD) 10,000–50,000 administrative fine for failure to hold meeting or submit resolutions; repeated non-compliance may lead to compulsory dissolution by MOEA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Annual Return and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of up to 3% of unpaid tax per 30-day delinquency (maximum 10%); interest accrues at 1.5% per month; tax lien and forced execution may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Tax (VAT) Return – Final and Adjustment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 April for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of TWD 1,000–10,000 for late filing; underpaid tax subject to 0.5% to 1% monthly surcharge and interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Uniform Invoice (Voucher) Turnover Return and Void/Issued Invoice Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the end of each 2-month period (six filings annually)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of TWD 3,000–30,000 per incident; repeated violations may trigger suspension of business operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registration Renewal of Vessel Towage/Salvage License and Port-State Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maritime Port Bureau, Ministry of Transportation and Communications
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal by license anniversary date (typically 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without renewal exposes company to administrative fines up to TWD 150,000 and suspension of towage/salvage operations until fully renewed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Companies Act-registered WFOEs must have financial statements audited and certified by a certified public accountant (CPA) prior to submission to the CIT authority, regardless of revenue size; additional quarterly or semi-annual CPA review may be required for listed/regulated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TFRS) based on IFRS; for small and medium enterprises, SME Financial Reporting Standards (SME FRS) may apply.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Company Act and Anti-Money-Laundering Act, the company must annually update the list of shareholders holding 10% or more and any natural-person ultimate beneficial owners (UBO) to the competent authority (MOEA) with the annual filing; changes in control after any share transfer must be reported within 15 days. Failure to file accurate UBO data triggers fines of TWD 100,000–500,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law, Article 4, standard rate for resident enterprises)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday applies to ISIC 5222 deep-sea towage and salvage. Potential preferential regimes: (1) 15% High and New Technology Enterprise rate if qualifying technology certification is held (unlikely for towage operations); (2) Small and Low-Profit Enterprise reduced 20% rate with effective 5% tax burden during 2023-2027 where taxable income does not exceed RMB 3,000,000, total assets do not exceed RMB 50,000,000, and employees do not exceed 300; (3) 100% super-deduction for qualifying research and development expenses on salvage technology. For a normalized profitable WFOE the effective rate is 25% plus 10% dividend withholding upon repatriation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Class A), main form A100000, e-filed through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (calendar year or approved non-calendar fiscal year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the fiscal year end (statutory deadline 31 May of the following year for a 31 December year end). Quarterly prepayments made during the year are credited against the final annual liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from deep-sea towage, marine emergency salvage, tug charter hire, standby vessel fees, and ancillary services per the audited financial statements prepared under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE files as a Chinese tax resident on worldwide income; revenue from towage/salvage performed in international waters is fully included, with Section A108010 used to claim foreign tax credits for taxes paid to other jurisdictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fuel, crew wages, vessel depreciation and amortization, repairs, port dues, towing gear, insurance, and direct subcontractor salvage costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs recharged by a Taiwan or third-country group entity must meet the arm's length standard under EIT Law Article 41; intercompany service fees without benefit evidence are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 (Total Book Profit, 利润总额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax derived from operating and non-operating income less expenses and losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carry into the tax calculation; book-tax differences are adjusted on attached schedules. Foreign currency income must be translated at the applicable People's Bank of China exchange rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 13 (Tax Adjustment Increase, 纳税调整增加额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate additions arising from disallowed deductions, excess depreciation, non-deductible entertainment and advertising expenses, and transfer pricing upward adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjustments imposed by the tax authority under GAAR or transfer pricing audits are reported here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 15 (Offset of Prior-Year Losses, 弥补以前年度亏损)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward and utilized in the current year, capped at 5 years from the loss year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the Chinese WFOE cannot be off-set against income of the Taiwan parent or other group entities; group relief is not available in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 23 (Taxable Income, 应纳税所得额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total book profit adjusted by increases, decreases, and loss offset, matched to minimum-tolerance taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Relevant deemed income for a towage vessel owned by a related offshore entity and operated by the WFOE may be imputed under substance and control rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% standard rate; 15% for High and New Technology Enterprises; 20% reduced rate (effective 5% for qualifying small low-profit enterprises).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE is a resident enterprise; the rate does not depend on profit repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 27 (Income Tax Payable, 应纳所得税额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable rate before incentives and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No tax sparing credit applies under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 31 (Tax Reduction and Exemption, 减免所得税额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Incentive amounts: environmental protection equipment deductions, venture capital exemptions, and R&D super-deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Towage-specific incentives are not available; claims require pre-filing technology registration documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 33 (Foreign-Source Income Tax, 境外所得应纳所得税额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chinese tax attributable to income from towage/salvage operations sourced outside mainland China.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes paid are creditable only for resident enterprises with documentary evidence; the Taiwan parent is not taxed currently on withholding unless dividend remitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 34 (Actual Payable, 实际应纳所得税额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net annual CIT payable after foreign tax credit and prepayments withheld in prior quarters.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any unpaid balance must be settled before an exit ban can be avoided by the legal representative.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return: RMB 2,000 fine, increased to RMB 10,000 for serious cases (Tax Administration Law Article 62); underpayment other than fraud: 0.05% daily surcharge on unpaid tax (Article 32) and a 50%-500% late-filing/underpayment penalty (Articles 63-64); fraudulent underpayment is subject to criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Quarterly Prepayment Return (Class A), form A200000, e-filed through the e-Tax portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 15 days after the end of each quarter (15 April, 15 July, 15 October, 15 January).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 (Cumulative Taxable Income for the Year, 本年累计金额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative taxable income computed on actual quarterly profits (or prior-year apportionment basis).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrual of international towage income is required in the quarter when services are performed, regardless of invoice timing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25%, 15% preferential, or 20% small-profit rate as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Rate must match the expected annual rate; under-withholding triggers surcharge interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 (Quarterly Tax Payable, 应补(退)所得税额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative prepayment computed after deducting prepayments of prior quarters.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' withholding is not credited here; the WFOE's own CIT prepayment is separate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late quarterly filing: RMB 2,000-10,000 per Article 62; underpayment of quarterly installments: 0.05% daily surcharge and a 50%-500% penalty where the under-declaration is deliberate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Report Form for Withholding of Enterprise Income Tax (扣缴企业所得税报告表), filed to the competent PRC tax authority, combined with treaty-benefit information reporting under SAT Announcement No. 35 (2019) via the e-Tax portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Event-driven: each dividend distribution, interest payment, or royalty payment to the Taiwan shareholder
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Withhold at source and remit the withheld EIT to the tax authority within 7 days from the date of payment (Tax Administration Law Article 39; dividend distribution date is the date of shareholders' resolution or actual crediting, whichever occurs first).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Block A (Withholding Agent Particulars, 扣缴义务人信息)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: WFOE name, unified social credit code, registered address, and competent tax authority.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE acts as withholding agent for the non-resident recipient; bank payment instructions must cross-match the filed return before foreign exchange release.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Block B (Non-Resident Payee Particulars, 非居民企业信息)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taiwan parent company name, Taiwan unified business number (tax ID), country of residence, and bank account details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan payee must be identified as resident of Taiwan for the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement claim; the Certificate of Tax Residence from Taiwan's Ministry of Finance (居住者证明) must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Block C (Gross Payment Amount, 收入额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross dividend amount resolved, gross interest or royalty contract amount before withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amounts reduced to nil after thin-capitalization recharacterization must be reported as deemed dividends with a 10% (or 5%) withholding rate; SAFE wire payment on Lloyd's standard form requires the same declared amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Block D (Withholding Rate and Exemption, 适用税率及减免)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory 10% provisional rate, or 5% under Cross-Strait Tax Agreement Article 10 for qualifying 25%-or-higher direct shareholders; 7% for interest and royalties under the Agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief is applied by the WFOE after collecting the Taiwan residence certificate and beneficial ownership declaration; the tax authority may deny relief on post-review if the Taiwan entity is a conduit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Block E (Withholding Date and Remittance, 扣缴日期)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date of actual payment or deemed distribution; remittance deadline seven calendar days thereafter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Failure to remit by deadline triggers the daily surcharge and potential foreign exchange control blacklisting.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold: 50%-300% penalty on the unwithheld amount (Tax Administration Law Article 69); failure to file the withholding return: RMB 2,000-10,000 fine (Article 62); failure to remit: 0.05% daily surcharge and freezing of bank deposits.
